distinguishing_features: Actively treats the wheel-seat fillet with ultrasonic impact rather than merely monitoring fatigue damage.
Generates a localized compressive residual-stress field to improve surface fatigue behavior without changing axle geometry.
Uses XRD residual-stress magnitude as an in-service acceptance and falsification metric.
Preserves the constrained axle geometry while introducing a localized mitigation process.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce fatigue-crack initiation risk at a geometrically constrained fatigue hot spot in a steel rail axle without redesigning its geometry or replacing the axle.
parsed.viable_reason: Although ultrasonic surface treatment can be feasible, the stated mechanism incorrectly treats a largely constant compressive residual stress as directly subtracting from the alternating stress range, and the proposed XRD-only test does not validate the claimed fatigue-life improvement.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Relative to the supplied monitoring-based prior art, applying localized ultrasonic impact to create compressive residual stress at the specific fillet is a distinct active mitigation mechanism rather than a routine parameter change.
